caption:
Nobody is more stressed in December than a man paying for the holidays with overtime and pretending he's fine. 👇

You're adding up the gifts in your head.
You took the extra shifts.
You can't leave the job, so you lean on it even harder.
And you've already decided to smile through it so nobody worries.

Here's what's really draining you:
It's not just the money.
It's carrying the money stress alone, while acting like everything's fine.

And you're not the only one. In a 2025 Modern Health survey, nearly 2 in 3 workers said they feel pressure to look happy during the holidays, even when they're not.

Why it matters: a man who carries it alone shows up to the holidays exhausted, short-tempered and somewhere else in his head. That's the part your family remembers.

The one fix: sit down with your partner this week and pick ONE holiday number together. Whatever fits, fits. No extra shifts to cover a number nobody agreed on.

Your kids won't remember what the gifts cost. They'll remember if you were there.

slides.big: If you can't describe yourself without your job title, this is for you.
slides.small: Your job owns more of you than it should.

Someone asks, "What do you do?"
And your whole answer is the job.
You can't remember the last thing you did just for you.

For years, the job took all your time.
So slowly, it became all of who you are.
That's why a bad day there feels like you're worth nothing.

Jobs end. Layoffs happen. Retirement comes.
If the job is all you are, the day it's gone, you're gone with it.

slides.big:
The fix:
Get one piece of you back.
slides.small:
Write down 3 things you are that have nothing to do with work.
Father. Fisherman. The guy who fixes things. Whatever's true.
This week, give ONE of them a full hour.

slides.big:
Work is what you do.
It was never who you are.
slides.small:
Save this for the next bad day at work.

caption:
The reason a bad day at work wrecks your whole week has nothing to do with the work. 👇

Someone asks, "What do you do?"
And your whole answer is the job.
You can't remember the last thing you did just for you.

You can't quit. Your family depends on that paycheck.
So the job took your time, then your energy, and slowly it became all of who you are.

That's why a bad review or a rude boss hits so hard. When the job is all you are, a bad day there feels like proof you're worth nothing.

You already know this is true. Think about how many conversations with other men start with "So what do you do?"

Why it matters: jobs end. Layoffs happen. Retirement comes. If the job is all you are, the day it's gone, you lose yourself with it.

The fix: write down 3 things you are that have nothing to do with work. Father. Fisherman. The guy who can fix anything. Then give ONE of them a full hour this week.

Look at this view. The road you're on is narrow, but there's a lot more out there than the path in front of you.

What are YOU besides your job? 👇
